title: Bram and the Winter
premise: Hazel Brightwater arrives at Blackfen School to teach the winter term and finds a class photo with faces no one remembers, plus a headmaster who insists the missing students were never enrolled. Her habit of documenting everything leads her to the founders' sleep recordings, where a second voice answers questions asked of sleeping children — a voice that begins answering hers. The ritual the founders began requires a witness who remembers, and Hazel is being groomed as its final instrument; loyalty to her students pulls against the truth that remembering them is what feeds the thing beneath the school. In the end she burns the archive mid-ritual, unmaking the children's recorded names to starve it, at the cost of her own memories of them — she leaves Blackfen whole but unable to say why she weeps at empty desks.
about_author: Q. M. Ishikawa is the pen name of a former boarding-school archivist who spent six years cataloguing institutional records before turning to fiction. They write horror about paperwork, memory, and the violence hidden in orderly systems.

chapters.title: Enrollment
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She arrives at snowbound Blackfen School, notices a class photo with blurred gaps, and starts her documentation journal as a comfort ritual. The headmaster, Mr. Vane, deflects her questions with practiced warmth. Emotional beat: uneasy belonging — she wants this fresh start badly enough to ignore the cold spots in the corridors.

chapters.title: The Sleep Recordings
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Assigned night duty, she plays the founders' old reel-to-reel sleep tapes for insomniac students and hears a second voice answering questions the children ask in their dreams. She documents it obsessively. Emotional beat: thrill curdling into dread — her prayer of documentation has summoned something that answers.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A boy named Tomas stops attending; records show he was never enrolled, yet Hazel has his essays in her own hand-graded stack. Other teachers recite the same denials with glassy calm. Emotional beat: gaslit isolation — only her notebook insists the boy existed.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, intercut with 1911 ledger entries. In the archive cellar she finds the founders' ritual: a bargain trading remembered children for the school's endurance, requiring a witness every fifty years. The winter solstice approaches. Emotional beat: horrified comprehension — the school itself is the predator's body.

chapters.title: Second Voice
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The voice on the tapes begins addressing her directly, using her childhood nickname no one at Blackfen knows, offering to return Tomas if she completes the rite. She records their conversations until the tape fills with her own voice replying. Emotional beat: seduction — power offered precisely to the powerless.

chapters.title: Loyalty
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Vane reveals he was once a teacher who finished half the ritual to save his own class decades ago, and warns her that refusal erased them anyway. Her remaining students, sensing danger, beg her not to leave before term ends. Emotional beat: divided heart — every choice betrays someone she's sworn to protect.

chapters.title: What the Snow Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Following the voice's map, she digs beneath the frozen quad and uncovers the founders' circle of name-stones, each carved with a child who 'transferred.' Touching one floods her with the child's final memory. Emotional beat: grief as evidence — the dead testify through her hands.

chapters.title: The Witness
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Solstice eve: Vane and the faculty bind her into the ritual as the required witness, revealing her hiring was orchestrated by the thing itself, which chose her because she cannot stop recording. The voice offers her the school's power if she speaks the closing words. Emotional beat: betrayal crystallizing into clarity — she was always the sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ash and Ink
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, climax. At the circle's center she understands the trap: completing or refusing both feed it, but destroying the record starves it. She burns the ledgers, tapes, and her own journals inside the ring, speaking each child's name aloud as it turns to ash so they exist once, freely, then let go. Emotional beat: terrible liberation — truth wielded as a weapon against memory-hoarding power.

chapters.title: Spring Term
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. Blackfen stands ordinary in thawing light; Vane is gone, the cellar sealed, the students intact though no one recalls what nearly happened. Hazel packs to leave, stopping at an empty desk where she cries without knowing why. In her pocket, a blank notebook. Emotional beat: bittersweet cost — she saved them by surrendering the proof she ever knew them.
